samples.summary: The new `requestLayoutRefresh` seam (measure-without-paint inside an open undo unit) has no test at all
samples.evidence: `text-editor.ts:734-740` now swallows every interior `requestRender()` and instead calls `this.requestLayoutRefresh?.()`; `editor.ts:2531` wires it to `recomputeLayout`. Nothing exercises this: grepping `requestLayoutRefresh` across the repo returns only the two source sites and doc comments — no test file. If the wiring were deleted (or the call inside the wrapper removed), every existing test would still pass, yet the rest of a unit reads a stale `getLayout()` (`blockParentMap` → `isInCell`/`getCellInfo`, which `applyPastePlan`/`insertBlocks` branch on, and wrap affinity). A paste or Enter inside a table cell reading a stale parent map is a wrong-destination write, i.e. content landing outside the cell. The frontend paint test (`editor-undo-selection.test.ts:363`) counts paints only; it never asserts a layout was refreshed mid-unit, and the docs package tests do not wire `requestLayoutRefresh` at all.

samples.summary: Enter / page-break / IME-commit / programmatic-paste paths were wrapped in `withUndoUnit` with no test covering their undo cost
samples.evidence: The diff converts five more composite actions to `withUndoUnit`: `handleEnter`'s cell branch (text-editor.ts:2651), its body branch (:2674), `handlePageBreak` (:2714), `pasteAsPlainText` (:4247) and the Hangul commit-over-selection path (:5882). The only editor-level undo-unit assertions added are for typing (`type('X')`), HTML paste, and Backspace (`editor-undo-selection.test.ts:340-388`). Grepping the frontend docs tests for `key: 'Enter'` finds only split/merge repro cases with no `getUndoStackForTest()` counting, and `handlePageBreak`/`pasteAsPlainText` appear in no test file. Pressing Enter over a select-all is exactly the #1045 shape (delete N blocks then split) — if that batch is dropped or the snapshot/batch ordering regresses there, the same >50-entry stack overflow silently destroys the tail of the document, and nothing in the suite notices.

samples.summary: The load-bearing rule "`saveSnapshot()` must be outside the unit or undo restores the post-edit caret" is documented but never asserted for the new units
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit`'s doc comment (text-editor.ts:3827-3837) makes this the second of two rules callers depend on, and `MemDocStore.batch()`'s adoption logic exists solely to make that ordering cheap. No test asserts caret/selection after undoing one of the new units: the only selection-restoration test is `editor-undo-selection.test.ts:130` for the toolbar `applyStyle` path, which does not go through `withUndoUnit`. The #1045 tests (`:340-388`) assert text content only, never `editor.getActiveSelection()`. Moving any `saveSnapshot()` inside a `withUndoUnit` body would keep the whole suite green while undo silently restored the post-edit caret.
searchedFor: Grep withUndoUnit call sites in text-editor.ts

samples.summary: The paint-deferral test counts an unattributed `ctx.save()` and covers only the typing path; the documented "replayed even after a throw" behavior is untested
samples.evidence: `expect(ctxCalls.save).toBe(1)` (line 366) infers paint count from an arbitrary 2D-context method on a proxy that counts every call by name; nothing pins that `paint()` calls `save` exactly once, so the assertion is a proxy for the property rather than the property, and it silently conflates any other single `ctx.save()` in the same tick. Additionally `withUndoUnit`'s comment (text-editor.ts:3823) claims the held render is replayed "including after a throw", but no test throws inside a unit and checks a render still happened — `memory.test.ts:561` covers only the store's re-arming, not the editor's replay.

samples.summary: The undo-floor-identity test asserts only the undo count, never that the document actually reverts, and never covers the `undoFloorMark === null` branch
samples.evidence: `expect(undone).toBe(50)` (line 385) counts `canUndo()`-driven iterations; it never checks the document content after the 50 undos, so a `canUndo()` that returns true while `undo()` no-ops or corrupts state would still pass. The new `markUndoFloor()` also has an explicit empty-stack branch (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:857`: `stack.length > 0 ? stack[stack.length-1] : null`) and the matching `if (this.undoFloorMark === null) return true` in `canUndo()`; no test constructs a store whose undo stack is empty at `setDocument` time, so that branch is unexercised.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: handleEnter's cell branch (text-editor.ts:2651), its body branch (:2674), handlePageBreak (:2714), pastePlainTextFromClipboard (:4247) and the Hangul commit path (:5882) are all newly wrapped saveSnapshot()+withUndoUnit composites. The only editor-level undo-cost assertions in the suite are in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts, and they cover HTML paste (:218-267), select-all+type (:335-372), Backspace (:374-386) and named-style redefinition (:466-495) — nothing dispatches Enter, Cmd+Enter, a plain-text paste or a composition commit while counting getUndoStackForTest(). Repo-wide greps for withUndoUnit/undoUnit in *.test.* return only that file plus the store-level contract tests in packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts:303-335; every `key: 'Enter'` test in packages/docs/test (link-trailing-edge:120, text-box-link-trailing-edge:101, table-link:97, editor-read-only:231) asserts split/link behavior with no undo counting; no e2e coverage exists. No counterexample found. Caveat on impact only: deleteSelection() opens its own unit (:3859-3866), so a regression on the Enter outer wrapper would cost 2 units, not the ~100 the finding implies — the gap is real but its worst case is smaller than described.

finding.summary: No test that a batch which genuinely writes DROPS redo — the negative half of the `priorRedo` restore is uncovered
finding.evidence: The delta moves redo-clearing out of `snapshot()`/`batch()` and into `willWrite()`, and `batch()`'s finally block restores `this.redoStack = priorRedo` only when `wroteNothing` (memory.ts:287-300). Every new/existing redo test covers the restore side: 'a batch that writes nothing leaves redo history intact' (line 382), 'a self-reverting batch leaves redo history intact' (line 402), 'snapshot() then a batch that writes nothing leaves redo intact' (line 440), and 'a write after an adopted empty batch still drops redo' (line 459 — the write is OUTSIDE the batch). I grepped every `canRedo` assertion in packages/docs/test (results: memory.test.ts lines 170,175,181,186,190,392,396,408,416,449,454,468,474) and none is of the shape `undo(); batch(() => { realWrite() }); expect(canRedo()).toBe(false)`. If the `wroteNothing` guard on the restore were ever wrong (e.g. restore made unconditional), the suite would stay green while a redo after a real batched edit reapplies a stale branch state over the document — silent data loss for the user.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists. packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts:421-443 ('a batch that writes drops redo history') does exactly `snapshot(); insertText(); undo(); expect(canRedo()).toBe(true); batch(() => insertText()); expect(canRedo()).toBe(false)` — the negative half of the `priorRedo` restore in memory.ts:287-300, and its comment says so verbatim. It further asserts the batched write landed ('Hello?') and that undo reverts, so it would fail if the `wroteNothing` guard were removed and the restore made unconditional. A second counterexample covers the adopted-checkpoint path at memory.test.ts:445-465 ('a batch that writes on an adopted checkpoint drops redo history'), asserting canRedo() === false after `snapshot(); batch(write)`. The finding's quoted grep line numbers for canRedo assertions do not match the current file (actual: 170,175,181,186,190,392,396,408,416,433,439,454,461,495,500), so its evidence was stale.
